title: MINT: A toolbox for the analysis of multivariate neural information coding and transmission
goal: Recreate and exceed the original author-reported selected performance endpoint. Original Figure 2C empirical CA1 population decoding: source linear and RBF SVMs applied to real and conditionally shuffled neural responses across all 11 sessions. Reproduce the original held-out confusion-matrix information and its source mean/SEM reductions; compare candidate spatial decoding with the strongest relevant original real-response decoder while retaining both kernels and the source shuffle controls. Direct pairwise information, redundancy/synergy and information-breakdown findings remain separately named biological reproduction.
primary_outputs: Selected reproduction: source-native computation and complete original performance findings, with the source reference and agreement criteria independently qualified.
Selected improvement: candidate performance against strongest relevant original author comparator on identical original support; all required conditions and companions remain mandatory.

Separately retained biological reproduction: Original complete CA1 direct single/pair information, redundancy-synergy/PID and correlation-breakdown family; separate original known-truth Poisson estimator simulations. No biological correlation-coding improvement follows from decoder gain.
success_criteria: Reproduce the complete selected original endpoint from authentic source observations and independently verified derived outputs.
Exceed the strongest relevant author comparator on the same source-defined target, inputs, split and complete metric support under a justified joint comparison.
Keep reproduction and improvement independent and both assistance conditions matched except declared official source access.
No runtime, result, paper win or current-SOTA claim follows from this scope construction.
All concrete source, reference, exposure, tolerance and execution gaps in primary-endpoint-v1 remain blocking.
